title: Alternative lithography defectivity (nanoimprint, DSA)
bottleneck: Nanoimprint lithography and directed self-assembly promise cheap patterning without EUV, but defectivity is the wall: template wear and particle contamination in imprint, and defect annihilation limits in DSA, keep defect densities far above HVM requirements. Overlay for imprint is mechanically challenging, and neither technique has a full ecosystem of resists, templates, and inspection.
why_it_blocks: A viable EUV alternative would break ASML's cost monopoly and democratize advanced patterning; without one, the entire industry's cost curve depends on a single vendor's tools. Competition in lithography is effectively zero.
current_state: Canon ships nanoimprint tools with improving defectivity, and DSA sees use in limited applications like contact-hole shrink. Neither is close to displacing EUV for leading-edge logic. Template lifetime in nanoimprint is measured in hundreds of wafers, far below the durability economics that photomasks enjoy.
